speaker_role: current admissions officers (named Isthier and Yulia, Swarthmore College Office of Admissions)
commercial_incentive: official college recruitment/marketing video for Swarthmore
key_insights: Swarthmore states it does not decide admission based on any single factor like class rank or test scores
Application review explicitly considers context: opportunities and resources available to the applicant, including high school curriculum options, geographic location, and lived experience

Gives a concrete rigor example: a student at a school offering only two AP classes who takes both is seen as having taken the most rigorous load available, even though that's far fewer APs than a student at a 30-AP school would be expected to take
States that access to test prep, extracurriculars, and advanced coursework varies significantly between students and is factored into review
Says Swarthmore is above all looking for intellectual curiosity, a passion for learning, and engagement with the world beyond campus
specific_numbers_or_facts: Example given: a school offering only 2 AP classes vs. a school offering 30 AP classes, used to illustrate contextual rigor evaluation
notable_or_distinctive: Gives a genuinely concrete illustration (2-AP-school vs. 30-AP-school) of how 'holistic, contextual' review actually gets applied to course rigor, rather than just asserting that holistic review exists.
reliability_notes: Official college marketing content, so naturally presents the admissions process in the most favorable light; the described criteria are self-reported policy, not independently verified, and specific to Swarthmore rather than generalizable to all schools.
